key_insight: HVOF-applied Ni-20Cr+40TiC produced the most oxidation-resistant coating on SA516 boiler steel, cutting high-temperature weight gain by 95.71% versus uncoated steel.
engineering_relevance: Dense Ni-Cr-based ceramic coatings can markedly improve boiler steel durability in cyclic 900°C oxidizing environments, making them promising for thermal protection of high-temperature components.
method: Prepared SA516 steel with Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings by HVOF and plasma spray.
Ran cyclic air oxidation for 50 cycles at 900°C.
Characterized phases and microstructure using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 50-cycle oxidation testing at 900°C, with the HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC coating showing the lowest mass gain and the uncoated steel suffering severe spalling and Fe2O3 formation.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated under laboratory cyclic oxidation; long-term service behavior, thermal shock, and adhesion under real boiler conditions still need validation.
paper_title: Microstructure and High-Temperature Oxidation Behaviour of HVOF and Plasma Sprayed Ni–Cr-Based Ceramic Coatings on SA516 Boiler Steel
